sentences.text: The Director is a greater expert and therefore the statute says that his certificate shall be accepted by the court as conclusive evidence.
For all purposes the report of the public analyst is replaced by the certificate of the Director.....
Superseded is a strong word.

It means obliterate, set aside, annul, replace, make void,
inefficacious or useless, repeal.
The Director's certificate supersedes the report given by the public analyst.
Once superseded it does not survive for any purpose.

It will be anomalous to hold that for some purpose it survives and for other purpose it is superseded."
8.3.1
From the above dictum, it is evident that as the Director, Central Food Laboratory is considered a greater expert, the Certificate issued by him is considered as final / concuslive.

sentences.text: In that case, the Food Analyst found the sample of compounded Asafoetida to be adulterated as it did not conform to the prescribed standard.
Whereas, the Central Food Laboratory vide its certificate found the sample to be in conformity with the prescribed standard.
The Ld.Magistrate declined to discharge the accused on the basis of the certificate of Central Food Laboratory.
Accused approached the Hon'ble High Court in revision.
The Hon'ble High Court accepted the contentions of the accused and quashed the prosecution proceedings.
The Municipal Corporation challenged the same before the Hon'ble Supreme Court.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court after considering the relevant provisions under PFA Act observed as under:
"9.....Sub section (3) of Section 13 is important in this context and is extracted below :
"The certificate issued by the Director of the Central Food Laboratory under sub section (2B) shall supersede the report given by the public analyst under sub section (1)."
10.When the statute says that certificate shall supersede the report, it means that the report would stand annulled or obliterated.

The word "supersede" in law, means "obliterate, set aside, annul,
replace, make void or inefficacious or useless, repeal", (vide Black's Law Dictionary, M/s Priya Dutt Sharma vs State, Through Commissioner, Department of Food Safety & Ors.
5th Edn.).
Once the Certificate of the Director of Central Food Laboratory reaches the court, the Report of the Public Analyst stands displaced and what may remain is only a fossil of it.
11.In the above context, the proviso to subsection (5) can also be looked at which deals with the evidentiary value of such certificate.

The material portion of the proviso is quoted below :

sentences.text:
"Provided that any document purporting to be a certificate signed by the Director of the Central Food Laboratory........shall be final and conclusive evidence of the facts stated therein."
12.If a fact is declared by a statute as final and conclusive, its impact is crucial because no party can then give evidence for the purpose of disproving the fact.
This is the import of Section 4 of the Evidence Act which defines three kinds of presumptions among which the last is "conclusive proof.

"When one fact is declared by this Act to be conclusive proof of another, the court shall, on proof of the one fact, regard the other as proved, and shall not allow evidence to be given for the purpose of disproving it."
13.Thus the legal impact of a certificate of the Director of Central Food Laboratory is threefold.

It annuls or replaces the report of the Public Analyst, it gains finality regarding the quality and standard of the food article involved in the case and it becomes irrefutable so far as the facts stated therein are concerned....."
M/s Priya Dutt Sharma vs State, Through Commissioner, Department of Food Safety & Ors. 8.5

sentences.text: 11.0 The appellant has further contended that no witness was examined by the Ld.ADM and the impugned order has been passed on the basis of the application under Rule 3.3.1(3) of FSS Rules filed by the FSO.
Perusal of the record shows that after notice, the appellant had appeared before the Ld.ADM and requested for time for filing reply and subsequently filed reply dated 10.01.2013.
Thereafter, the matter was reserved for orders after hearing the parties.
Nothing prevented the appellant from the summoning/examining any witness he wished to.
No such request was however made.
Nor was any such averment made in his reply before the Ld.ADM.
Evidently, the plea has been raised at the appellate stage only for the sake of argument.
12.0 The appellant has also contended that the sanction has been granted by the Designated Officer without application of mind.

Ld. Chief Public Prosecutor on the other hand, submitted that the M/s Priya Dutt Sharma vs State, Through Commissioner, Department of Food Safety & Ors. Designated Officer granted the sanction to prosecute the FBO only after duly going through the documents of the case.

sentences.text: 12.1 Perusal of the sanction order dated 18.10.2012 on record, shows that the Designated officer granted the sanction after going through the facts/documents which is reflected in sanction order.
13.0 In view of the above, the appellant has failed to demonstrate any procedural lapses, as pleaded.
14.0 In view of the above, it has come on record that the sample food article did not conform to the specified standard as laid down in Regulation 2.1.1(1) FSS (FPS & FA) Regulations.

Non conforming to the specified standard rendered the sample food article/toned milk sub standard in terms of Section 3(1)(zx) of FSS Act which reads as under:

"3.Definitions (1).....
(zx)substandard  an article of food shall be deemed to be substandard if it does not meet the specified standards but not so as to render the article of food unsafe;"
M/s Priya Dutt Sharma vs State, Through Commissioner, Department of Food Safety & Ors. 14.1 It may be mentioned that Sections 26 FSS Act which lays down the responsibilities of the FBO, inter alia enjoins upon every FBO, to ensure that food article, whether produced, sold, distributed, stored etc. under his control shall satisfy the requirements of the FSS Act and the Rules and Regulations framed thereunder.

entities.text: Priya Dutt Sharma vs State, Through Commissioner, Department of Food Safety & Ors. 14.1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Section 26 FSS Act reads as under:
"26.Responsibilities of the food business operator.(1) Every food business operator shall ensure that the articles of food satisfy the requirements of this Act and the rules and regulations made thereunder at all stages of production, processing, import,
distribution and sale within the businesses under his control.
(2)No food business operator shall himself or by any person on his behalf manufacture, store, sell or distribute any article of food (i) which is unsafe; or (ii) which is misbranded or substandard or contains extraneous matter....."

14.2 From the plain reading of the above provision, it is evident that the appellant violated Section 26(2)(ii) FSS Act by storing/selling sub standard toned milk/ sample food article which was meant for sale for human consumption.
Such a violation is punishable under Section 51 FSS Act which provides for a maximum penalty of Rs.Five Lakhs.
15.0 No averment regarding quantum of penalty has been M/s Priya Dutt Sharma vs State, Through Commissioner, Department of Food Safety & Ors. made by the appellant.

Appeal is according, dismissed.

From the above dictum, it is evident that as the Director, Central Food Laboratory is considered a greater expert, the Certificate issued by him is considered as final / concuslive.
The word "supersede" in law, means "obliterate, set aside, annul,
replace, make void or inefficacious or useless, repeal", (vide Black's Law Dictionary, M/s Priya Dutt Sharma vs State, Through Commissioner, Department of Food Safety & Ors.
5th Edn.).
Once the Certificate of the Director of Central Food Laboratory reaches the court, the Report of the Public Analyst stands displaced and what may remain is only a fossil of it.

The Hon'ble court while relying upon the decision of the Hon'ble Apex court in Andhra Pradesh Grain & Seeds Merchant Association v. Union of India, AIR 1971 SC 246 and Chetumal vs State of M.P., AIR 1981 SC 1387, held that:
"7.....Proviso to Section 13(5) also indicates that what is stated in the later certificate issued by the Director would be final and conclusive evidence of the facts stated in the said certificate.....Once this type of conclusive evidence emerges on record,
whatever might have been contraindicated regarding the concerned ingredients of the sample as found in the prior report of the public analyst would be totally pushed out of the arena of contest and cannot be looked at.

the appellant has simply made a bald averment that such variation shows that the sample was not taken in a proper manner and was not representative.
Perusal of the record shows that neither was any specific submission made in this respect nor was any material produced by the appellant in this regard, before the Ld.ADM.
The appellant did not even make any M/s Priya Dutt Sharma vs State,

Thus, the appellant failed to make any specific submission much less demonstrate through evidence, that the variations in two reports was substantial enough so as to conclude that the sample was not representative.
Thus, the appellant can hardly be granted benefit on account of variation in the reports.
